title: Streaming chat messages can result in large data transfer
rationale: Facts: maintainer wch reports that streaming a 5800-byte response transferred 3.5MB from the Python process to the browser, and includes a runnable ollama-based repro app plus a breakdown of per-chunk versus wrapper overhead; proposes text-diffing or throttling as fixes. A 2024-08-27 maintainer comment (cpsievert) notes Python's difflib.ndiff() as a candidate approach, but no fix has shipped as of this scan (issue remains open, untouched since 2024 until surfacing in this window). Classification hypothesis: performance/needs-clarification issue -- the repro is concrete but no acceptance criteria or committed design exists yet, and the issue overlaps conceptually with the O(n^2) reporting concern raised independently in #277 without being an exact duplicate (that issue is about full-transcript resend on settle; this one is about per-chunk streaming growth). Duplicate check: searched the 25 most recently updated shinychat issues; no other open issue covers streaming bandwidth specifically, and this is related to but distinct from #277 -- not linking as a duplicate since the mechanisms differ (streaming chunk growth vs. settled-transcript resend). Wrong-location check: shinychat owns the chat streaming transport; correct repo. Regression check: no evidence this changed from an older release; it appears to be inherent to the current design, so no regression label. Reproduction plan: already included in the issue body (ollama chat app with instrumentation). Impact: affects any app streaming non-trivial response lengths, worse for long or widget-heavy chats; a design fix (diffing/throttling) is known but unimplemented. Priority: Medium -- valid, well-defined performance issue with a clear repro and moderate impact, but no workaround-free production breakage. Recommended next action: label Priority: Medium and needs clarification (no committed design/acceptance criteria yet) and mark ai-triage:done; not risky to close out triage since no aggressive label (e.g. regression, Critical) is being asserted.

title: Chat client re-sends the full message transcript on every settle (O(n^2) reporting)
rationale: Facts: maintainer cpsievert documents that since the chat UI moved to a client-authoritative model (PR #272), the client resends the entire settled-message transcript on every settle point, producing O(n^2) total bytes over a session, worse for widget-heavy chats carrying repeated htmlDeps; the issue includes precise code references (js/src/chat/state.ts, ChatApp.tsx, shiny-transport.ts, and the Python/R consumers) and four candidate designs (append-delta protocol, content-addressed messages, session-level htmlDeps table, or accept/cap) without committing to one, explicitly raised as a follow-up scoped out of #272. Classification hypothesis: performance/design issue needing a scope decision among the four listed options, not a concrete bug encountered in production. Duplicate check: related to but distinct from #281 (per-chunk streaming growth vs. this issue's settled-transcript resend); not an exact duplicate of any other open issue in the 25 most recently updated. Wrong-location check: correct repo, this is the chat client/server reporting protocol shinychat owns. Regression check: not a regression -- this is the intended (if costly) consequence of the #272 architecture change, not an unintended behavior change from an older release. Reproduction plan: no runnable repro needed; the growth is a mathematical consequence of the documented design, and acceptance criteria are already specified in the issue (linear, not quadratic, growth). Impact: real but gradual -- scales with conversation length and widget usage, not an acute failure. Priority: Medium -- well-defined, evidenced scaling concern with moderate impact and a menu of viable fixes, but no immediate production breakage. Recommended next action: label Priority: Medium and needs clarification (design choice among the four options is still open) and mark ai-triage:done; not risky since no aggressive label is being asserted and the maintainer already scoped the follow-up work.
